md.areas: far southeast Pennsylvania into New Jersey
md.summary: The threat of hail and perhaps a tornado will persist as storms move east across the Delaware River.
md.discussion: A line of storms with a tail-end supercell is expected to persist into central NJ where the air mass remains sufficiently unstable. Temperatures have warmed, with some mixing of the dewpoints into lower 50s F, down from mid 50s F earlier. Low-level shear per TPHL VWP shows around 100 m2/s2 0-1 SRH, also down from earlier today. Cold temperatures aloft will continue to support hail. Tornado potential is more conditional given current trends, but storms intersecting the east-west front over northern NJ may experience some enhanced rotation potential there. VWPs to the south from KDOX and KLWX show gradually veering of the low-level winds, with additional storm formation south of the existing activity becoming less likely as drying moves in the the west.

layers.label: Rivers right now vs normal
layers.caption: Current NWM streamflow percentile: High (>95th) through Low. This is the 'ground truth' a flash-flood watch rides on - saturated basins here means the next storm floods faster.

layers.label: 5-day high-flow outlook (AEP)
layers.caption: NWM-NBM blend, peak streamflow over the next 5 days, as annual exceedance probability: 2% = a 50-year-ish peak, 10% = 10-year, 50%/threshold = nuisance-to-minor flooding possible.

flooding.note: Streamflow layers are NOAA National Water Model graphics (water.noaa.gov); QPF outlooks are WPC. The NWM paints entire river networks - empty rivers are normal outside flood events.

weekly.label: Weeks 1-2 precipitation
weekly.caption: North America precipitation anomaly, model weeks 1-2. Blues = wet signal, browns = dry. This is the rain CFSv2 expects in days 1-14.

weekly.label: Weeks 1-2 temperature
weekly.caption: North America surface-temperature anomaly, model weeks 1-2. This is the temperature CFSv2 expects in days 1-14 - same style as the CPC 6-10/8-14 outlooks, but straight from the model.

weekly.label: Weeks 3-4 precipitation
weekly.caption: North America precipitation anomaly, model weeks 3-4 (days ~15-28).

weekly.label: Weeks 3-4 temperature
weekly.caption: North America surface-temperature anomaly, model weeks 3-4.

cfsv2.note: CFSv2 is NOAA's coupled ocean-atmosphere model run 4x daily to ~9 months. Weekly panels are North America means/anomalies for model weeks 1-4; monthly panels are ensemble-mean anomalies + probability plumes for the calendar month. Skill decays with lead - treat week 3-4 and monthly as trends, not weather.

variables.label: Temperature
variables.caption: Three-month mean 2 m temperature anomaly. Warmer colours = the model favours above-normal temperatures for that span, cooler = below.

variables.label: Precipitation
variables.caption: Three-month mean precipitation anomaly. Green = wetter than normal, brown = drier than normal for that span.

cansips.note: CanSIPS is Environment and Climate Change Canada's seasonal prediction system; its two coupled models (CanESM5 and GEM-NEMO) are members of the multi-model ensemble CPC publishes. Seamless multi-model agreement is the useful signal; a single model's tilt at months 3-6 is a lean, not a forecast.
